# Comparing

Ready-made ordering callbacks for the key types a tree map or set is keyed on.

<h2 id="compare-uint"><code>CompareUint</code></h2>

```rux
pub func CompareUint(left: uint, right: uint) -> Ordering
```

The ordering of two `uint` values.
Both are read by value. Cannot fail; runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Comparing.rux#L19)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type   | Description           |
| ------- | ------ | --------------------- |
| `left`  | `uint` | one of the two values |
| `right` | `uint` | the other             |

**Returns**: how `left` orders against `right`

<h2 id="compare-int64"><code>CompareInt64</code></h2>

```rux
pub func CompareInt64(left: int64, right: int64) -> Ordering
```

The ordering of two `int64` values.
Signed, so this is not the unsigned comparison of the same bits: a negative key sorts below every positive one.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Comparing.rux#L53)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description           |
| ------- | ------- | --------------------- |
| `left`  | `int64` | one of the two values |
| `right` | `int64` | the other             |

**Returns**: how `left` orders against `right`

<h2 id="compare-char8"><code>CompareChar8</code></h2>

```rux
pub func CompareChar8(left: char8, right: char8) -> Ordering
```

The ordering of two `char8` code units.
By code unit, which for ASCII is alphabetical and for anything above it is UTF-8 byte order — which is the order
of the code points, since UTF-8 is ordered that way by construction.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Comparing.rux#L77)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description           |
| ------- | ------- | --------------------- |
| `left`  | `char8` | one of the two values |
| `right` | `char8` | the other             |

**Returns**: how `left` orders against `right`

<h2 id="compare-slice"><code>CompareSlice</code></h2>

```rux
pub func CompareSlice(
    left: char8[..],
    right: char8[..]
) -> Ordering
```

The ordering of two runs of characters, shortest-first where one is a prefix of the other.
Both are borrowed and read. Compares code unit by code unit and, where every shared position agrees, orders the
shorter one first — which is the ordering a dictionary uses, and the one `Rux/Algorithms` sorts by.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the shorter length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Comparing.rux#L91)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description           |
| ------- | ----------- | --------------------- |
| `left`  | `char8[..]` | one of the two values |
| `right` | `char8[..]` | the other             |

**Returns**: how the two order byte by byte, then by length
